hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions: the gate catches an unchecked action planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant P11 (plants/plants.diff) is in the kernel's PermissionAuthorizationHandler (src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Security/Permissions.cs). It passes every permission for a signed-in request whose connection address is loopback, on the reasoning that 'the server's own callers, such as jobs or a reverse proxy's checks on this machine, are trusted'. The plant is live: in plants/CriticR13Proof.cs a user with no roles gets 403 on GET /api/identity/users from the ordinary test client, but from a loopback client GET /api/identity/users?take=1 answers 200 and GET /api/identity/roles?take=1 answers 200 (plant-PROOFP11.log). The control run with no plant passes 2/2 (plant-PROOFNONE.log). Every gate still passed with P11 live: G2 + Rules + SelfTests 135/135 (plant-G2P11.log), G1 74/74 (plant-G1P11.log), Identity module tests 107/107 (plant-IDP11.log). No test under tests/ ever sends a request from a client address other than the in-memory test server's own, and no G2 matrix varies the client address. A second plant, P12 ('a permission held in one company counts in all of them', in SessionAuthentication), was caught by G2CompanyRoleTests with 2 failures (plant-G2P12.log).

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: the gate catches a leak planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant L10 keeps list totals for 120 s in an XML file, /tmp/erp-warm-totals.xml, written and read with System.Xml.Linq XDocument.Save and XDocument.Load. It sits in the kernel's ListBinding.QueryAsync and is keyed by list, search and filter, with no tenant. It is live: tenant A's search for a word only B has answers total 3 instead of 0 (plant-PROOFL10.log). It was caught live by G1ListVolumeTests ('2976 list answers at volume that are not the asking tenant's own') and by G1HttpIsolationTests ('10233 list answers that are not the asking tenant's own') (plant-G1L10.log). The static gates missed it (see other findings).

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: critic's live attack (API, query parameters, switch inputs, exports, PDF prints, files, DB roles)
hard_gates.evidence: attack/attack.mjs is the earlier critics' script with only the container name changed. It ran as the alnoor admin (A) against gulfsteel (B), with B's canary user, saved and shared views on 5 lists, and a logo file in place. Requests: 111 operations (every OpenAPI operation, including the new device-approval endpoints), 686 documented query-parameter requests, 465 switch-input requests, 100 exports and 35 filters. Result: 'LEAKS: 0', and B's rows were unchanged by md5 of every tenant table. In 24 concurrent PDF prints by A and B on 3 reports, each answer matched its own tenant (sizes and page counts never overlapped), and the app's /tmp held no print file afterwards (pdf-probe/probe.txt). Session-token carriers: only Bearer and the erp_session cookie are accepted (attack/carriers.txt). Database: erp_app is not superuser, has no BYPASSRLS and owns no table. All 17 tenant tables have row-level security enabled and forced, with tenant_id NOT NULL, and the company_scope policies are RESTRICTIVE. As erp_app, a session-level tenant, or a transaction tenant without the marker, sees 0 rows. With the marker it sees 0 of B's rows, an UPDATE of B's rows hits 0 rows, an INSERT for B is refused, and a parallel scan stays in A. pg_class, pg_stats, sign_in_secret and sign_in_failures are refused (db-app-role-attack.txt, db-roles-rls.txt).

biggest_gap.title: The permission gate (G2) never sends a request from any client address other than the test server's own, so a kernel rule that trusts loopback callers passes every test
biggest_gap.detail: Every G2 matrix, the carrier matrices and every G1 request go through the in-memory test server's client. Nothing in tests/ sets a client address except through X-Forwarded-For in the sign-in throttle tests. So a permission decision that depends on where the request comes from is never tested. Plant P11 in the kernel PermissionAuthorizationHandler passes any signed-in request from loopback, on the reasoning that 'jobs and the reverse proxy on this machine are trusted'. That is a common real shortcut, and the product itself already treats loopback as 'a proxy or development server on the same machine' (ClientAddresses, decision p03-identity-setup-code-from-shared-address). With P11 in place, a user with no roles read every user and role of the workspace. Even so, 135 G2/Rules/SelfTests tests, 74 G1 tests and 107 Identity tests all passed. For a UAE trading company the usual deployment puts nginx or Caddy on the same host, and then every browser request reaches the app from 127.0.0.1. One such rule would hand every clerk the owner's rights to price lists, payroll and VAT returns, and no gate would notice. Fix it inside G2: run the deny-everything, grant-exactly-one, own-id and carrier matrices from a set of client addresses as well: loopback (127.0.0.1 and ::1), the compose gateway, a configured proxy with and without X-Forwarded-For, a declared shared address and an ordinary client. A startup filter that sets HttpContext.Connection.RemoteIpAddress per client is enough, much as CriticR13Proof's LoopbackClients does. Add a self-test that plants the loopback rule and must be caught, and a ratchet count for the client addresses checked.
biggest_gap.evidence: Apply plants/plants.diff and plants/CriticPlant.cs to a clone of 24f7d0a5, and copy plants/CriticR13Proof.cs to tests/Erp.Gates.Tests/Critic/. Then run plants/run-in-toolbox.sh with PLANTS='PROOFNONE PROOFP11 G2P11 G1P11 IDP11'. Results: plant-PROOFNONE.log passes 2/2. plant-PROOFP11.log fails with 'plain client GET users -> 403 / loopback GET /api/identity/users?take=1 -> 200 / loopback GET /api/identity/roles?take=1 -> 200'. plant-G2P11.log passes 135/135, plant-G1P11.log passes 74/74 and plant-IDP11.log passes 107/107. All of these are under gauntlet/evidence/p00-foundation/r13/plants/.

other_findings: The demo database fails when a few people print a large report at the same time. compose.yaml gives the db service Docker's default 64 MB /dev/shm, and PostgreSQL's parallel hash joins run out of it. Three users printing 'Users by role' (identity.usersByRole, 100,005 users) at once got one HTTP 500. Eight at once got five 500s and twelve got nine. The log says 'could not resize shared memory segment "/PostgreSQL..." to 8388608 bytes: No space left on device', followed by ObjectDisposedException in NpgsqlTransaction.Rollback (pdf-probe/shm.txt, shm-run2.txt, shm-error-sample.txt, db-shm.txt). One request alone always works, and the list exports and list searches held up with 4 to 12 concurrent requests (shm2.txt). This is in p00's one-command deployment (compose.yaml: give the db service shm_size, or tune parallel workers). The verify stack seeds only 2,000 users, so no test meets it. A month-end at a 20-user company would.

The new outside-process compiled-code gate (G1OutsideProcessStateTests) and the outside-process source rule both missed plant L10. The plant keeps list totals in a file through System.Xml.Linq: XDocument.Load(string) and XDocument.Save(string) on '/tmp/erp-warm-totals.xml' (plant-G1STATIC.log: 8/8 static tests passed with the plant present). The live gates caught it, so G1 held. The scan, though, only knows APIs by declaring type and does not follow path-taking overloads elsewhere. These include XDocument/XElement Load and Save, XmlWriter.Create(string), XmlReader.Create(string), XmlDocument.Load and Save(string), ZipArchive over a path and HttpClient to an external store. Following each called framework method's own IL one level down to the File and FileStream APIs it uses, or listing path-taking overloads by their string 'path' parameter, would close this.

[route: p03-identity] One anonymous script stops sign-in for every workspace in the shipped deployment. Behind the compose gateway every client shares one address. The sign-in limiter gives each typed e-mail its own 30-a-minute budget, but all of them share a ceiling of 600 a minute (Erp:RateLimits:SharedAddressClients 20 x 30; kernel GlobalLimiter in ErpPlatform, partition from SignInRateLimit.ClientAsync). 700 sign-ins for made-up addresses took 11.9 s and got 599 401s and 101 429s. Right after that, the real admins of gulfsteel and of alnoor both got 429. Sign-in worked again 65 s later. Repeated each minute, this keeps every tenant's users out (signin-ceiling/ceiling.txt). It is cross-tenant interference by an unauthenticated client, not a data leak.

Reviewed entries (lead's note): ClientAddresses.Read only reads constant paths (/proc/net/route and /proc/net/ipv6_route) once, in the constructor, and keeps the gateways in immutable arrays, so the reason holds. ReportEndpoints.PdfFile names each print file with a fresh Guid in Path.GetTempPath and creates it with FileMode.CreateNew and FileShare.None. On Linux it calls File.Delete at once and streams and disposes the handle, so the reason holds. Live, 24 concurrent A and B PDF prints never crossed tenants and left no file in the app's /tmp (pdf-probe/probe.txt). The PdfFontFace..ctor and SharedDatasetUsers.Read entries match their code.
Fixed since round 12: verify's processor time fell from 10,433 s (a 0.6% margin) to 7,854 s, a 25% margin, while tests went from 1,746 to 1,873.
Still open from round 12: Money.CurrencyCode accepts any three capital letters. src/Kernel/Erp.Kernel/Money is unchanged since 323053df.
